caption:
Anthropic plans to sell up to $3.5 billion of its shares to investors in Japan as part of its US IPO, a Japanese filing shows, according to Reuters.
That is more than the $2.2 billion Japanese investors got in SpaceX's record IPO in June.
The filing does not give the IPO's total size, price or valuation.

paragraphs.text: Anthropic plans to sell up to 552.9 billion yen of shares, about $3.5 billion, to investors in Japan as part of its public listing in the United States, according to a Japanese filing that Reuters reported from Tokyo on November 2, 2026. Reuters converted the figure at a rate of 157.82 yen to the dollar.

According to the filing, the new shares sold to investors in Japan will raise working capital and fund operating expenses and capital expenditure. The filing does not state the overall size of the IPO or the valuation Anthropic is seeking, Reuters reported.
A larger Japan tranche than SpaceX

Reuters compared the plan with the SpaceX IPO in June, the largest listing on record, in which investors in Japan secured $2.2 billion of the $75 billion raised. Anthropic's ceiling for Japan is roughly 1.6 times that amount, a comparison FourWeekMBA also drew in its analysis of the filing.

FourWeekMBA noted that the yen figure is an upper limit rather than a final allocation, and that the amount actually placed in Japan will not be known until the offering is priced. Reuters did not name the Japanese brokers handling the tranche.

Anthropic, PBC filed a registration statement on Form S-1 with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on October 26, 2026, for a proposed initial public offering of its Class A common stock. The company said it has applied to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT, and that the number of shares and the price range have not yet been determined.
The company named Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley as the firms from which copies of the preliminary prospectus may be obtained.

According to FourWeekMBA, the S-1 describes public offerings outside the United States in Australia, Canada, certain European Economic Area member states, Japan, Switzerland and the United Kingdom, while stating that Anthropic does not intend to list its shares on an exchange in those places. The filing says that if any foreign offering is dropped, those shares are expected to move to the remaining offerings, so the total size of the deal is not expected to change.

Some investors have discussed a valuation of about $1.5 trillion for Anthropic, according to earlier Reuters reporting. The company has not confirmed a figure, and the price range in its US filing is still blank.

In NeuraFeed's reading, a dedicated tranche of this size suggests Anthropic expects demand for its shares well beyond US institutions. Selling directly to investors in Japan and five other jurisdictions spreads the offering across more buyers, which can help a company place a very large deal without leaning only on American funds.

The next filing to watch is the amended S-1 that sets a price range and share count. That document will show the total amount Anthropic plans to raise, and from there how large a share of the deal the Japan ceiling of about $3.5 billion represents.
